messages:
Samantha (Support): Hey team, customer (acct: acme-corp) seeing repeated 502s on /v1/generate around 2024-06-12T14:02Z. They provided request_id `req_20240612_7b4f9a` and another `req_20240612_7b52e1`. Can SREs look up server logs? They report latency spike then 502.

Priya (SRE): Got it. Any quick repro steps from the customer? If they can paste a curl with an X-Request-ID header that would help isolate. I'll start a log search for that request_id.

Samantha (Support): Quick repro curl I asked them to run: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Request-ID: req_20240612_7b4f9a" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate``` They ran it twice; the first succeeded, second returned 502 with no body.

Priya (SRE): Running Datadog/Kibana queries now. Initial Datadog filter: `service:redwood-inference AND request_id:req_20240612_7b4f9a` — in Kibana try `request_id:\"req_20240612_7b4f9a\"`. Note: prod hot logs retained ~30d, cold indices ~90d; if the request is older it may be in cold/archived indexes.

Marta (Backend): I pulled the trace for `req_20240612_7b4f9a` — saw a timeout calling the GPU worker: `ERROR runtime-proxy: upstream timeout after 120000ms -> returning 502` Stack: router -> runtime-proxy -> gpu-worker-22. Trace id `trace-8d2f`. Looks like the worker dropped the connection while waiting for kernel allocation.

Priya (SRE): Exact Elasticsearch query I used: ```GET /logs-*/_search?q=request_id:\"req_20240612_7b4f9a\"&size=100&sort=@timestamp:desc``` Also narrow by time: `@timestamp:[2024-06-12T13:58:00 TO 2024-06-12T14:10:00]`. If nothing shows up, check `logs-archive-*` and increase `size` or use the trace id.

Marta (Backend): Additional note: if you need the GPU worker logs, query the node logs for `gpu-worker-22` around that timestamp: `host:gpu-worker-22 AND message: \"req_20240612_7b4f9a\"`. We keep node-level logs in hot for 30d, cold for 90d, then they roll to S3 archive where retrieval can take a few hours.

Samantha (Support): Thanks — customer also wants explanation whether this was an infra glitch or auth/billing. They confirmed key was valid (acct acme-corp). Also asked for a debug bundle they can share.

Marta (Backend): To generate a debug bundle internally: `redwoodctl collect-debug --request-id req_20240612_7b4f9a --output /tmp/acme-req-req_20240612_7b4f9a.zip` (requires infra role). The bundle includes traces, logs, and kube events for the window. If you don't have CLI access, I can generate and upload to the ticket: s3://redwood-support-debug/acme-corp/1718209342-dbg.zip.

Priya (SRE): Suggested short customer reply: "We found a GPU-worker timeout for that request_id; we're investigating kernel allocation pressure. Can you repro with a fresh X-Request-ID and paste the full response headers (or the curl -v output)? That will give us the new request_id to look up immediately."

Samantha (Support): I'll send that to the customer now and ask them to include the full `curl -v` output. Will post any new request ids here. :thumbsup:
